questions.question: Name the three types of neuron and the direction of each, then write the five-part pathway for withdrawing a hand from a hot pot, naming the structure at each step.
questions.expected_answer: Sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors towards the central nervous system; motor neurons carry impulses from the central nervous system to effectors; interneurons connect them within the brain and spinal cord. Pathway: heat and pain receptors in the skin of the finger, sensory neuron, spinal cord (interneuron), motor neuron, muscles of the arm (effector) which contract and withdraw the hand.

questions.question: Give the function of the cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla and spinal cord, and explain why damage to the medulla is usually fatal.
questions.expected_answer: Cerebrum: conscious thought, memory, learning, senses and voluntary movement. Cerebellum: balance, posture and coordination of movement. Medulla: involuntary control of heart rate, breathing and blood pressure. Spinal cord: carries impulses between brain and body and is the centre for reflexes. Medulla damage stops the control of breathing and heartbeat, so death follows.

questions.question: Explain how a reflex action differs from a voluntary action and why reflexes are valuable, then describe how alcohol affects the nervous system.
questions.expected_answer: A reflex is rapid, automatic and completed mainly in the spinal cord without a conscious decision; a voluntary action passes through the cerebrum where a decision is made, which takes longer. Reflexes protect the body from damage by removing the delay. Alcohol slows the passage of impulses across synapses, lengthening reaction time, impairing judgement and disrupting the cerebellum's coordination, so balance fails and driving becomes dangerous.
